sources.entry: Cronicle - Simple, distributed task scheduler and runner with a web based UI. (Source Code) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Cronicle is a multi-server task scheduler and runner with a web-based UI, described as a fancy cron replacement written in Node.js.
summary.what_it_does: Cronicle schedules repeating, scheduled, and on-demand jobs across any number of worker servers and shows real-time job status with a live log viewer. A primary server keeps time and assigns jobs to workers, with automated failover to backup servers and auto-discovery of nearby servers. Jobs can be simple shell commands or plugins written in any language that read and write JSON to communicate with Cronicle. It records CPU and memory usage per job and provides historical stats with performance graphs. It also offers a REST API for scheduling and running events, API keys for external apps, and web hooks for notifications.
use_cases: monitor job logs and resource usage in a web UI
trigger jobs remotely via REST API
failover scheduled tasks to backup servers
notable: Primary/backup/worker server model with automated failover
Plugins can be written in any language using JSON messaging
Per-job CPU and memory tracking with historical graphs
README states xyOps is the successor and Cronicle now receives only maintenance
caveats: README says Cronicle receives maintenance only (bug fixes and security patches); new features are directed to xyOps
README does not include install commands; installation is covered in separate documentation files
